dispatch_path.finding: The dispatcher iterates the 6-byte pending groups, follows the original pointer array, obtains the original 27-byte record pointer, reads its opcode and dispatches it in place.

lifecycle_conclusion.finding: For the bound runtime path, 27-byte action records are loaded from WORLD, retained by pointer, shallow-scheduled by count+pointer-array reference, and dispatched in place. No copy/normalization step is present between WORLD deserialization and opcode execution in this path.
lifecycle_conclusion.producer_boundary: The complete PUZZLES/ROOMS -> WORLD producer/compiler remains HOLD.
lifecycle_conclusion.tail_implication: The varying +17..+26 bytes observed in v114 are already present in serialized WORLD and survive unchanged into dispatch. Their exact authoring origin remains upstream/HOLD; the audited runtime path does not manufacture them.

next_target: Audit static construction/mutation patterns outside the load/schedule/dispatch path: generic copies of 27 bytes, stores to +17..+26 near action-building code, and any indirect reachability into the paired WORLD writer.

population_path.boundary: Does not exclude indirect calls, generic/variable-size allocators, stack/static construction, or external authoring code.
population_path.finding: In the audited direct-call/immediate-allocation classes, the WORLD reader is the only population path for the nested 27-byte and 37-byte pointer lists and the only direct malloc(27)-style allocation.

shallow_runtime_schedule.finding: On condition success, runtime scheduling stores only the original 27-byte-list count and pointer-array address in a 6-byte pending group. It does not copy the 27-byte records.
